label: <DEL> or first m/t at steps 3-5, when sequence starts with d/b/h/3/f/y
predicate: ((phase == 1) | ((phase == 0) & isin(in_tok, [tok("m"), tok("t")]) & (in_first == 1))) & (t >= 3) & (t <= 5) & isin(first_tok, [tok("d"), tok("b"), tok("h"), tok("3"), tok("f"), tok("y")])
explanation: Fires almost only on a few trigger inputs: the <DEL> step (58% of mass) and first occurrences of m or t in the original phase (39%), with small amounts on w/i. On dev, (DEL or first m/t) alone gets recall 0.94 and mass recall 0.97 but precision 0.06: the trigger is necessary but not enough. Firing is gated by context. It is concentrated at steps 3-5 (short prefixes; rate drops sharply for L >= 7 and t >= 7) and strongly boosted when the first original token is d, b, h, 3, f or y (these are also the first output at <DEL>). Adding those conditions raises precision to ~0.43 with recall ~0.42 (dev F1 0.42). The top activations (~0.18) are <DEL> steps after short sequences starting with d or 3, or m/t right after i. Earlier tokens like i, 3, f, d also raise the odds. Essentially silent in the copy phase (0.7% of mass), at t=0, and on repeated tokens (in_first=0). The remaining dependence is graded and spread across the whole prefix, so it is not fully captured.
